9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium close-up, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) faces her reflection with the lipstick at her mouth and one hand holding an earring, her expression concentrated., Locked beauty framing through the mirror, Scarlett (Image 2) centered against white tile with the black turtleneck creating graphic contrast; warm sunlight catches her face and coral lips., INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM — MORNING. Hard sunlight cuts across white tile and a black stone sink. Scarlett (Image 2), a sharp-eyed city influencer in a black turtleneck, tears open a coral lipstick carton with one hand while her phone buzzes beside it. The handheld camera drifts with her movement as she catches the tube before it rolls into the sink., morning, downtown_apartment_bathroom_white_tile_black_stone, Hard morning sunlight enters through the window, creating crisp geometric highlights and strong shadows. A bright reflection travels across the lipstick's satin surface and illuminates Scarlett (Image 2)'s face at the mirror., White tile, matte black stone, black clothing and accessories, silver metal accents, vivid coral lipstick, and a small green accent from the hair clip., scarlett_city_influencer, Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
